newsitem.title: FRANCE: Frenchman, Irishman probed in Paris over IRA link.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman, Irishman probed in Paris over IRA link.

text.p: A French anti-terrorism magistrate opened a probe on Friday into a Frenchman and an Irishman on suspicion of aiding the IRA in its battle to end British rule in Northern Ireland, judicial sources said.

Frenchman Franck Lebret-Richer, 33, and Irishman Paul MacGarrigle, 39, were formally placed under investigation and ordered detained for "criminal conspiracy tied to a terrorist enterprise" by magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere, they said.
Lebret-Richer was suspected of having housed one or several militants of the Irish Republican Army IRA), which ended a 17-month truce a year ago.
MacGarrigle, an Irish citizen born in Belfast and suspected of being an IRA member, was also placed under investigation for violating arms laws after police said he was carrying a pistol.
He had been a long-term resident in France, where he worked in a cafe. A French judicial source said that MacGarrigle had previously been sentenced to jail terms in Ireland.
The two were among seven people detained on Wednesday in Paris, Arbois in the Jura and in the Seine-Maritime area near the capital. The others have since been released.

The seven were detained with help from information after a Frenchman, Jean-Louis Becker, was detained in northern France in October on suspicion of sheltering an IRA militant and for supplying him with false identity papers.

Becker was in turn detained afer information from British police who launched probes after an IRA bombing in Manchester in June that injured more than 200 people and virtually destroyed a shopping centre.
